title: Rheology by Shayok Misha Chowdhury and Bulbul Chakraborty at Playwrig...
transcript: Rheology is a scientific area of study, but here it's an experimental new theatre piece by Shayok Misha Chowdhury and his real-life mother, physicist Bulbul Chakraborty, about contradictions and in-betweens. It begins as a physics lecture about sand, a fragile solid whose exact behavioral definition has been elusive for years. Similarly hard to pin down is human behavior and how we respond to the forces thrust upon us. This piece evolves from something educational into something more experimental, a meditation on time, mortality, and preemptive grief. Although none of us can predict how certain losses will impact us until they happen, we can hypothesize — and in a theatrical context, we can experiment or simulate. As this piece navigates dualing concepts such as life and death, liquids and solids, or lecture and performance, we the audience experience a plethora of colors. I found it funny, poignant, and genuinely educational. A beautifully original piece that could have only been made by two people who are remarkably close but very different. Rheology is running at Playrights Horizons through May 16th. With that, another program for my collection.
